1988 S C M R 1283(1)

Present: Muhammad Afzal Zullah and Saad Saood Jan, JJ

NIMAT ALI Petitioner

versus

Mst. HAFEEZ BIBI and others‐‐Respondents

Civil Petition No.831 of 1987, decided on 11th May, 1988.

(From the judgment dated 6‐10,1987 passed by the Lahore High Court, Lahore in Writ Petition No.1427/87).

West Pakistan Family Courts Act (XXXV of 1964)‐‐

‐‐‐S.5‐‐Constitution of Pakistan (1973), Arts.185(3) & 199‐‐Suit for dissolution of marriage‐‐Ex parte decree upheld in appeal and Constitutional petition‐‐Order impugned‐‐Even if for some reason orders of Family Court and Appellate Court were set aside, circumstances of case were such that Khula' would be granted to wife‐‐No purpose, held, would be served by driving parties to another round of litigation‐‐Petition dismissed.

Ch. Mushtaq Ahmad Khan, Advocate Supreme Court and S.Abul Aasim Jafri, Advocate‐on‐Record for Petitioner.

Nemo for Respondents.

Date of hearing: 11th May, 1988.

ORDER

SAAR SAOOD JAN, J.‐‐An ex parte decree of dissolution of marriage was passed against the petitioner by the Family Judge. He made an application plication for setting aside the decree but the application was dismissed. He filed an appeal before the Additional District Judge which met the same fate. He then approached the High Court in constitutional jurisdiction, challenging the legality of the judgments of the Additional District Judge and the Family Court Judge but again he remained unsuccessful He now seeks leave to appeal from this Court

2. After hearing the learned counsel, we do not think that this is a fit case where leave should be granted. Even if for some reason the orders of the Additional District Judge and the Judge Family Court are set aside, the circumstances are such that Khula' would be A granted to respondent No.l. No purpose would be served by driving the parties to another round of litigation. Leave is refused.

M.I./N‐73/S Petition dismissed.
